crime.value: Murder of rape suspect by gunshot (two shots); central question: who killed the man and will the crime be solved or concealed?
crime.quote: Two shots, just like Greg said. One near the bottom of his gut. One in the neck.

victim.value: Accused rapist out on bail; 'killable' because he sexually assaulted Jenny (a police officer), was released on bail, and threatened to expose the assault, destroying her career and reputation.
victim.quote: He said vile things about what he'd done to her. He said he'd tell everyone in prison.

closed_world.value: Isolated house on Nine Mile Road near Missoula, Montana; snowed in during winter weather, limiting outside observation and escape routes.
closed_world.quote: The snow was sticking heavily...whatever tracks had been made by her husband's tires had been smoothed over by a perfect layer of white.

culprit_and_motive.value: Greg Sutton (Jenny's husband) commits the murder; motive is rage and the belief that justice has failed—the rapist is 'getting away with it' on bail; Greg seeks retribution.
culprit_and_motive.quote: He's winning...He did this to you, and nothing's happening. He's getting away with it.

investigator.value: Jenny Sutton, the rape victim and police officer; she investigates and conceals her husband's crime through forensic manipulation, evidence planting, and false reporting to authorities.
investigator.quote: She walked to the phone and dialed a cell phone number she knew by heart...Then she told Wayne the story.

suspect_architecture.value: Single perpetrator (unnamed rapist); Greg as secondary actor who commits the murder; Jenny as architect of cover-up. No false suspects — moral complexity distributed across three figures differentiated by role: victim, avenger, orchestrator.
suspect_architecture.quote: Greg stood, leaving Jenny on her own in the bed. 'I don't understand. How could they let this happen to you?'

red_herring.value: Jenny constructs a false narrative for Wayne Harvey — that the rapist called the house, made threats, and that Greg drunkenly went to confront him — redirecting suspicion from premeditated cover-up to a crime-of-passion domestic response.
red_herring.quote: The man called the house during dinner. He said vile things... Greg started drinking. She was at the Nine Mile house now and needed his help.

clue_fairness.value: The reader is shown all forensic steps Jenny takes in real time — fired rounds replaced, boots stepped in blood, tarp burned, temperature manipulation of body — before any investigator arrives, allowing reader to reconstruct the frame.
clue_fairness.quote: She held her familiar pistol and added two cartridges to fill the magazine. She fired two shots into a nearby tree.

social_world.value: Rural Montana law enforcement hierarchy: female patrol officers are marginal, decoy duty is gendered and dangerous, institutional loyalty (Wayne, Anne Lawson, Judge Parker) governs what gets pursued or buried. The mill-worker husband sits outside this power structure entirely.
social_world.quote: Jenny was one of two female patrol officers under the age of thirty-five working for the Missoula County Sheriff's Department.

alibi.value: Greg's alibi is constructed by Jenny: she ensures gunshot residue transfers to herself, burns his clothes, plants his coat at the scene, and manipulates time-of-death by cooling then rewarming the body, making her presence — not his — the forensic story.
alibi.quote: If they analyzed for gunshot residue, Greg would not be the one to test positive.

reveal_mechanic.value: The reveal is withheld from in-story investigators but fully demonstrated to the reader through Jenny's methodical, itemised cover-up actions — the two replacement cartridges, the boot-blood transfer, the body temperature manipulation — which expose the frame's architecture without any detective figure perceiving it.
reveal_mechanic.quote: The chill had kept the body fresh enough. Time of death wouldn't pose a problem.

media_and_audience.value: Institutional audience only — no press depicted. The story Jenny tells Wayne and Anne Lawson will become the official narrative absorbed by the County Attorney's Office and the Sheriff's Department; professional courtesy and sympathy for a violated colleague ensure it will not be scrutinised.
media_and_audience.quote: She needed Anne Lawson from the County Attorney's Office to come out, too.

investigator_wound.value: Jenny is simultaneously the investigator and the victim: her wound is the rape itself, which she must suppress, manage, and instrumentalise. Her professional competence is the mechanism of her psychological survival — and of the cover-up — creating an irresolvable tension between justice and self-preservation.
investigator_wound.quote: For just a moment, only a moment, she felt her heart quicken with a strange sense of pleasure.
